newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Enterprise to start $18 mln Romania drilling.
newsitem.headline: Enterprise to start $18 mln Romania drilling.

text.p: Britain's Enterprise Oil Plc will launch the second phase of an exploratory drilling project in the Romanian Black Sea shelf next week on the same block where it found gas, a company executive said on Wednesday.
"Our intention is to start the first well on February 18," Martin Macfadyen, general manager of Bucharest-based Enterprise Oil Exploration Ltd, told Reuters.

He said the move followed extensive re-evaluation of data as well as reprocessing of the seisimic information gathered by the company on Bloc 15, about 100 km northeast of Constanta, over the past two years.

Macfadyen said Enterprise would drill up to three wells on Bloc XV, where an exploratory well drilled by the company found gas in 1995. Tests in one reservoir interval produced a flow rate of 17.5 million cubic feet a day of dry gas.

"Our estimates put spendings for the three wells in the region of $18 million," he said, addding that drilling was expected to be performed with the jack-up rig Atlas owned by Romania's Petrom SA oil exploration and production company.
"We hope to sign the contract with Petrom tomorrow," Macfadyen said.
The Atlas is one of seven such rigs used by state-run Petrom for drilling and production purposes in the Black Sea, the Marmara Sea and the Gulf.
Enterprise has been active in the Black Sea since 1991, when it got licences in blocks XIII and XV offshore Romania as well as in Bulgarian offshore blocks II and VI.

Some local experts see Romania's Black Sea shelf as a promising area for new oil deposits. The country now obtains some 15 percent of its total crude output through its single drilling and extraction unit in the Black Sea.

Macfadyan also said Enterprise had not entered bids in a tender called by Romania last year covering exploration and production rights on 15 new blocks. Of these, 14 are onshore and one offshore on the Black Sea shelf. Their size varies from 500 to 2,000 square kilometres.
"We didn't see anything particularly attractive in the area on offer," Macfadyan said.
Last month, Enterprise completed testing an exploration well in block XV about part of a $45 million exploration project in Romania.
